action_criteria.expected_evidence: Polyradiculoneuropathy pattern (demyelinating or axonal features, absent F-waves, sural sparing where present); may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Nerve conduction studies and needle EMG
action_criteria.rationale: Nerve conduction studies support the diagnosis and separate an acquired demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy from a length-dependent drug or metabolic neuropathy [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Albuminocytological dissociation: raised protein with cells <5/mm3 (5-50/mm3 compatible but prompts an alternative; >50/mm3 suggests another diagnosis); protein may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Lumbar puncture for CSF cell count, protein and glucose
action_criteria.rationale: CSF supports the diagnosis and, in a transplant recipient, excludes the opportunistic infections and lymphoproliferative disease that raise the cell count [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: CSF CMV PCR not detected, with 2 cells/mm3 and a negative blood CMV PCR on valganciclovir prophylaxis
action_criteria.label: Optional CSF CMV PCR on triple immunosuppression
action_criteria.rationale: CMV polyradiculitis is the opportunistic mimic in a transplant recipient, but valganciclovir prophylaxis, a recent negative blood CMV PCR and an acellular CSF already make it very unlikely, so the CSF PCR is optional.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL (renal impairment that shapes IVIg and valganciclovir dosing) and magnesium 1.6 mg/dL; normal potassium, liver tests, albumin and CK
action_criteria.label: Baseline blood tests: full blood count, renal function and electrolytes, liver tests, albumin, glucose and CK
action_criteria.rationale: Routine blood tests give the baseline before IVIg; renal function matters more than usual on tacrolimus [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC in L, % predicted and mL/kg, MIP and MEP, with the trend; ICU-level monitoring if FVC <20 mL/kg or <60% predicted, MIP weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP <40 cmH2O, a fall of more than 30%, or bulbar weakness with weak cough
action_criteria.label: Bedside respiratory function (FVC, MIP, MEP), repeated serially while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Weakness is still progressing and spreading to the arms 4 months after lung transplantation; serial FVC, MIP and MEP decide when ICU-level monitoring is needed [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Continuous telemetry with blood pressure monitoring: sinus rhythm 68-96 bpm and blood pressure 104/62 to 152/90 mmHg, lowest after sitting up, in the first 24 hours; autonomic instability (rate and blood pressure lability, bradyarrhythmia) requires continued monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.label: Continuous inpatient cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Orthostatic dizziness suggests autonomic involvement, which can cause bradyarrhythmias and blood-pressure lability; monitoring continues while weakness progresses [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal sinus rhythm 86 bpm with normal intervals (QTc 442 ms) and no conduction or repolarisation abnormality: a baseline on tacrolimus while autonomic involvement can still develop
action_criteria.label: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
action_criteria.rationale: A baseline 12-lead ECG screens for autonomic dysrhythmia and conduction abnormality and gives the QTc before treatment [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Tacrolimus adds nephrotoxicity to IVIg and is little removed by plasma exchange; valganciclovir needs the renal dose for his creatinine clearance; trimethoprim raises potassium and creatinine
action_criteria.label: Check the transplant regimen (tacrolimus, mycophenolate, prednisone, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, valganciclovir) for interactions before IVIg or plasma exchange
action_criteria.rationale: A nephrotoxic calcineurin inhibitor with IVIg, a renally dosed antiviral and immunosuppressant handling during plasma exchange change how treatment is given.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on immunotherapy in GBS; not needed for the diagnosis or the treatment decision
action_criteria.label: Optional literature search on IVIg versus plasma exchange in GBS
action_criteria.rationale: Background evidence only; not a clinical step of the work-up.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not stop or reduce the transplant immunosuppression to treat GBS (rejection risk).
Do not add corticosteroids for GBS: oral corticosteroids are strongly advised against and IV methylprednisolone is not recommended [EAN_PNS_2023]; his maintenance prednisone continues.
Do not start IVIg without checking renal function.
required_recommendations: Admit to a monitored (high-dependency) bed with FVC, MIP and MEP every 4-6 hours; move to ICU-level monitoring if FVC falls below 60% predicted or 20 mL/kg (about 1.6 L at 80 kg), MIP becomes weaker than -40 cmH2O, MEP falls below 40 cmH2O, FVC falls by more than 30%, or bulbar weakness with weak cough develops [EAN_PNS_2023, Lawn_2001].

Start IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total, about 32 g/day at 80 kg) now, within 2 weeks of onset, because he cannot walk unaided (GBS disability score 3); with creatinine 1.4 mg/dL on tacrolimus use a sucrose-free product, a slower infusion rate and hydration, and check creatinine daily. Plasma exchange is equally effective and not contraindicated; it is a second choice here because of central-line infection risk on triple immunosuppression [EAN_PNS_2023].
Continue tacrolimus, mycophenolate and maintenance prednisone unchanged and agree the plan with the transplant team; recheck the tacrolimus trough and replace magnesium.
Adjust valganciclovir to the renal dose for his creatinine clearance (about 59 mL/min: 450 mg daily) with the transplant team.
Continuous cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses (orthostatic dizziness).
Pharmacological DVT prophylaxis (subcutaneous low-molecular-weight heparin) while he cannot walk [Leonhard_2019].

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome, AIDP, after lung transplantation

differential.key_features: Reported with calcineurin inhibitors and immune-mediated in mechanism, so it presents and is treated like GBS; troughs have stayed within target for 4 months, which makes it less likely but does not exclude it. Reassess if he relapses.
On valganciclovir prophylaxis, blood CMV PCR not detected 10 days ago, CSF CMV PCR not detected and only 2 cells/mm3 (CMV polyradiculitis gives a neutrophilic pleocytosis).

differential.diagnosis: Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder with nerve root involvement
differential.key_features: Blood EBV PCR not detected, acellular CSF with negative cytology, symmetric rather than multifocal deficits.
Cannot be excluded at presentation; progression beyond 8 weeks or 3 or more treatment-related fluctuations would point to it. Reassess at 8 weeks.
Uncomplicated postoperative course 4 months ago and no ICU stay before onset; demyelinating rather than axonal NCS.

key_clinical_evidence: Bilateral leg-predominant weakness with arm involvement and depressed reflexes progressing over 12 days, CSF albuminocytological dissociation (protein 76 mg/dL, 2 cells/mm3) and a demyelinating NCS: Brighton level 1 once the course plateaus within 4 weeks [Brighton_2011].

Transplant recipients have competing causes of neuropathy (opportunistic infection, drug toxicity, lymphoproliferative disease), but GBS occurs on immunosuppression and is diagnosed on the same criteria.

IVIg and plasma exchange are equally effective [EAN_PNS_2023]; plasma exchange is not contraindicated after transplantation and removes little tacrolimus, but IVIg avoids central venous access on triple immunosuppression and is the practical first choice.
Tacrolimus with renal impairment calls for a sucrose-free IVIg product, slower infusion and daily creatinine, and renally dosed valganciclovir.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Progressive bilateral weakness with depressed reflexes, CSF albuminocytological dissociation with 2 cells, negative CMV PCR in blood and CSF and a demyelinating NCS define GBS in a transplant recipient; immunosuppression does not prevent it.
red_herrings.data_point: Recent bilateral lung transplant on tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisone
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors on calcineurin-inhibitor neuropathy or an opportunistic infection, or suggests that GBS cannot occur on immunosuppression.
red_herrings.location: Medication list and past medical history

sequence_constraints.reason: Creatinine and magnesium are needed to judge the tacrolimus and valganciclovir interactions and the IVIg infusion plan.

interactions: Tacrolimus: nephrotoxic; adds to the risk of acute kidney injury from IVIg, especially with sucrose-containing products (use a sucrose-free product, slower infusion and hydration; monitor creatinine). Tacrolimus also causes renal magnesium wasting.
Tacrolimus: largely bound to erythrocytes and plasma proteins, so little is removed by plasma exchange; check trough levels during a course (relative caution).
Mycophenolate mofetil: no interaction with IVIg; highly albumin-bound mycophenolic acid may be partly removed by albumin-replacement plasma exchange (monitor).
Valganciclovir: renally cleared; the label dose for CMV prophylaxis is 450 mg daily at creatinine clearance 40-59 mL/min and 900 mg daily at 60 mL/min or more.
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole: raises potassium and serum creatinine (trimethoprim blocks tubular creatinine secretion).
Prednisone: no interaction with IVIg or plasma exchange; raises glucose.
general.proposed: IVIg or plasma exchange with tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, prednisone, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and valganciclovir
general.summary: Category-level review of the transplant regimen against IVIg and plasma exchange.
warnings: Plasma exchange needs large-bore central venous access; catheter-related infection risk is higher on triple immunosuppression (relative caution).

ecg.interpretation: Normal sinus rhythm, rate 86. Normal intervals (QTc 442 ms). No acute ST-T wave changes.

labs.interpretation: Hemoglobin 13.4 g/dL (low). Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL (elevated). Glucose 132 mg/dL (elevated). Magnesium 1.6 mg/dL (low). CRP 11.2 mg/L (elevated). ESR 38 mm/hr (elevated). Tacrolimus trough 9.8 ng/mL (within target). Remaining values within reference ranges.

results.finding: Guidelines for adults with GBS who cannot walk unaided advise IVIg 2 g/kg over 5 days within 2 weeks of onset or plasma exchange within 4 weeks, with no preference between them; corticosteroids are not advised.
A second IVIg course in patients with a poor predicted prognosis did not improve outcome and caused more serious adverse events.

general.summary: IVIg or plasma exchange is advised for adults with GBS unable to walk unaided; neither is preferred, and a second IVIg course is not advised [EAN_PNS_2023, Walgaard_2021].

metadata.difficulty_description: GBS in a bilateral lung transplant recipient: tacrolimus neuropathy, CMV and PTLD compete, and renal impairment on tacrolimus shapes how IVIg is given; plasma exchange is a relative, not absolute, caution.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 6 required actions, 1 red herring; opportunistic and drug-related mimics in an immunosuppressed patient and drug interactions that change dosing.
metadata.revision_reason: Reviewer 2 GBS audit: spine MRI is optional and limited to five cases with a concrete cord, traumatic, postoperative or infiltrative alternative; generic hidden MRI reports removed.

patient.chief_complaint: Twelve days of progressive leg weakness with dizziness and difficulty walking, 4 months after bilateral lung transplant on triple immunosuppression.

past_medical_history: Bilateral lung transplant 4 months ago for end-stage COPD, uncomplicated postoperative course

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. F. is a 66-year-old man who underwent uncomplicated bilateral lung transplantation 4 months ago for end-stage COPD and takes tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil and prednisone, with tacrolimus troughs between 8 and 12 ng/mL at clinic. Twelve days ago he noticed dizziness on standing and weakness of both legs. The weakness has progressed steadily: he needed a cane after 4 days and now cannot walk without support from two people. From day 5 he has had tingling of the feet and fingertips, and over the last 3 days his hands have felt weak when opening jars. At his transplant clinic visit 10 days ago his reflexes were normal and blood CMV and EBV PCR were not detected. He reports no recent infection, diarrhoea, immunization or new medication, and no bladder or bowel symptoms, back pain, double vision or swallowing difficulty.
